shots.line: Before we go back to that night, here's how this ended in court.
shots.what: real photo: Pike County Courthouse, Milford; chapter lettering types on

shots.line: The trial came in April twenty-seventeen in Pike County.
shots.what: real photo: the prosecution team walking to court; date types on

shots.line: Alex Douglass testified.
shots.what: his official portrait

shots.line: On April nineteenth, the jury convicted Eric Frein on
shots.what: real photo: Frein led by a trooper at the trial

shots.line: all twelve counts, including first-degree murder of a law enforcement officer and terrorism.
shots.what: typed card

shots.line: Then came the penalty phase to decide whether he'd live.
shots.what: real: camera crews behind police tape outside court (station caption cropped out)

shots.line: On April twentieth, Bryon Dickson's widow, Tiffany Dickson, testified about raising their two sons without their father.
shots.what: Cpl. Dickson's portrait, held (no photos of his family are used)

shots.line: Frein's parents testified too, asking for his life.
shots.what: real photo: the courthouse, closer

shots.line: On April twenty-sixth, the jury returned a death verdict.
shots.what: real: the District Attorney outside the courthouse after the verdict; name tag types on

shots.line: They found no mitigating circumstances.
shots.what: typed card

shots.line: The judge formally imposed the sentence the next day.
shots.what: real: Tonkin, punched in

shots.line: Remember that recorded statement from the night of the arrest?
shots.what: typed card; chapter lettering

shots.line: The jury heard Frein's confession.
shots.what: real photo: Frein at the trial, pushing in

shots.line: Two years later, Pennsylvania's highest court said the jury should never have heard it.
shots.what: the court opinion: highlighter on the court's name and "DECIDED: April 26, 2019"

shots.line: Frein had repeatedly told investigators he wanted to stop talking.
shots.what: opinion p. 28: highlighter on "unambiguously invoked his right to remain silent on multiple occasions"

shots.line: They kept going.
shots.what: opinion p. 28: highlighter on "the officers continued to question Appellant"

shots.line: The rifle from the hangar fired the bullets that killed Dickson and wounded Douglass.
shots.what: opinion p. 29: three highlighter sweeps (the bullets, the rifle, the hangar)

shots.line: Frein's DNA was on it.
shots.what: opinion p. 29: highlighter on "Appellant's DNA was on the rifle"

shots.line: The handwriting on the torn pages was his.
shots.what: 3D object: the three torn pages

shots.line: The court ruled that the confession hadn't changed the verdict.
shots.what: typed card

shots.line: The conviction stood, and so did the death sentence.
shots.what: typed card

shots.line: In January twenty-twenty, the US Supreme Court declined to take the case.
shots.what: typed card

shots.line: Pennsylvania set an execution date for June twenty-second, twenty-twenty.
shots.what: typed card (the WTAJ clip for this line is a long close-up of his face from the perp walk, so it is not used)

shots.line: Ten days before it, a Pike County judge put the execution on hold so Frein could continue challenging his conviction and sentence.
shots.what: typed card

shots.line: Pennsylvania hasn't carried out an execution since nineteen ninety-nine.
shots.what: typed card
